Incorporating the Beige Book alongside the July 2020 SLOOS changes the balance of risks. While SLOOS flagged widespread tightening in bank credit and softer loan demand (especially C&I, CRE, and most consumer segments), the early-September Beige Book reported modest-to-moderate gains in activity from depressed levels, with notable strength in housing and autos, improving manufacturing, and gradual employment gains—albeit still below pre-pandemic levels and with high uncertainty. Combined with the FOMC’s highly accommodative stance (ZLB, ongoing Treasury/agency MBS purchases, and new average inflation targeting), the Beige Book’s evidence of a continuing rebound softens the purely negative tilt from SLOOS. Credit supply frictions and weak demand outside housing still pose downside risks, but real-side momentum is improving.

Net: Still slightly negative given credit constraints and pandemic uncertainty, but less so than an SLOOS-only read.
